doc.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022

title: Berklee's status and the later Artist's Diploma
summary: He did not graduate in his time at Berklee; years later, through Herb Pomeroy, he got an Artist's Diploma and the school soon dropped its DownBeat ads.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. All right. So I’m going to jump ahead just a little bit. You get to Berklee in its early years, was it an accredited school at the time or just a —
It was a college. And was it a degree program for you?

I didn’t stay long enough to graduate. I graduated much later, many years later. It’s a long story but Berklee never recognized my contributions. And I’d been noticing at the time DownBeat was having all these ads, one page ads, with pictures of their graduates,

recommending the school. I thought gee, what about me? You know? So I called up the school and the music department said, “Well you have to finish your courses.” I said, “Well I’ve got a hundred recordings out you know, how many more do I need to get a degree you know?” So the guy, the head of the department, said, “Why don’t you talk to Herb.” So I called Herb and Herb set me up with what they call a star — what do they call it, hold on, an “Artist’s Diploma” which means you finished school in two years. So he gave me that without me having to graduate.
And the next month they discontinued their ads.
